subject: Reasoning
description: Venn diagram set relations: which figure best represents categories

questions.stem: Which Venn diagram BEST represents 'Birds, Pigeons, Animals'?

options.option_text: Three disjoint circles for all groups
Pigeons inside Birds inside Animals
Two overlapping circles only used
Three circles all overlapping each

questions.explanation: Pigeons ⊂ Birds ⊂ Animals (each contained in next). So innermost = Pigeons, then Birds around it, then Animals outermost. CONCENTRIC nesting (each circle inside the next, no overlap with outside categories). Common SSC RC pattern: identify the hierarchy first.
questions.subject: Reasoning

options.option_text: All three concentric inside each other
Doctors + Engineers as 2 circles inside Humans
All three completely separate disjoint
Doctors and Engineers fully overlap

questions.explanation: Doctors ⊂ Humans + Engineers ⊂ Humans, but Doctors + Engineers MAY OVERLAP (some people are both — dual qualifications). So: large Humans circle, with Doctors + Engineers as 2 smaller circles inside, slightly overlapping (or non-overlapping if no overlap stated). Distractor 4 wrong — they don't fully overlap.

options.option_text: Cricket + Football inside Sports (no overlap)
All three are shown as the same single circle
All three completely separate non-touching
Cricket inside Football inside Sports nested

questions.explanation: Both Cricket + Football are types of Sports, but disjoint from each other (no game is both). So: outer circle Sports; two non-overlapping inner circles for Cricket + Football.
questions.subject: Reasoning

options.option_text: All 3 separate disjoint circles, no overlap
Mothers + Daughters overlap, both in Women
Mothers inside Daughters inside Women here
Mothers and Daughters fully overlap as one

questions.explanation: All Mothers + Daughters are Women → both subsets of Women. Mothers + Daughters OVERLAP (a person can be both — a woman can be a daughter of her mother + a mother of her own children). So: Women is outer; Mothers + Daughters circles overlap inside.
questions.subject: Reasoning

options.option_text: Chair inside Table inside Furniture
Chair + Table as 2 circles inside Furniture
All three identical circles overlapping
All three separate disjoint circles

questions.explanation: Chair + Table are types of Furniture (both ⊂ Furniture). They are DISJOINT (a chair is not a table, vice versa). So: Furniture outer circle; Chair + Table inner non-overlapping circles.
questions.subject: Reasoning

options.option_text: All three concentric inside each other (nested)
Three overlapping circles (boy/student/player overlap)
All three completely separate circles, no overlap
Boys inside Students inside Players nested fully

questions.explanation: None of these is a strict subset of another: not all boys are students; not all students are players; not all players are boys. They overlap in various ways. Some boys are students; some students are players; some boys are also players + students simultaneously. THREE overlapping circles, with 7 regions (1 alone in each + 3 intersections of two + 1 of all three + 1 outside).

options.option_text: All three as separate disjoint circles
Mumbai inside Maharashtra inside India
All three with full overlap of regions
Mumbai inside India only, ignoring Maharashtra

questions.explanation: Mumbai ⊂ Maharashtra ⊂ India (each strictly inside the next, no overlap with outside). CONCENTRIC nesting, like Indian Russian dolls. Same pattern: 'Country, State, City' / 'Continent, Country, State' / 'Solar System, Earth, Asia'.
